payload.text: Camera coordinates in the virtual camera plane are radially symmetrical to the projection plane and share the same sign as world coordinates.
Virtual camera coordinates simplify image analysis by avoiding inversion and aligning with world coordinates, making projections easier to interpret.

- Camera coordinates in the virtual camera plane. The camera projection plane is behind the pinhole and at a distance $f$ of the origin. Let the coordinates in the camera projection plane, $x$ and $y$, be parallel to the world coordinate axes $X$ and $Y$ but in opposite directions, respectively. For simplicity, it is useful to create a virtual camera plane that is radially symmetrical to the projection plane with respect to the origin and it is placed in front of the camera (\[a\]). This virtual camera plane will create a projected image without the inversion of the image. The coordinates in the virtual camera plane will have the same sign as the world coordinates, that is, with the same $x$,$y$ coordinates (i.e., both images are identical apart from a flip).
